metadata.note: The Wisconsin and Michigan Railway (inc. 26 Oct 1893): Peshtigo / Peshtigo Harbor, Wis. - Bagley Junction - Koss - Faithorn Junction (Soo Line) - Norway - Quinnesec - Iron Mountain, Mich., with trackage over the Milwaukee Road Bagley Jct - Marinette - Menominee and a Western Division Everett - Miscauno Island - Holmes Junction - Walton. Regular passenger trains 1894 - c.1918 (drawn to 1917); a single proven 1920 year after the 1918-1920 shutdown; abandoned 1938. Every feature is W&M-operated: Walsh control (1900), Clearing House administration (1905), Marsch's tax-sale purchase (1910), receivership (1912-17) and Marsch's purchase (1917) changed ownership, not the operator, and wartime federal control falls in the 1918-1920 gap - so there is no Rule 4 ownership split. Not to be confused with the 1870s 'Wisconsin & Michigan Railroad' (Green Bay - Pike, later Milwaukee and Northern / Milwaukee Road), the Wisconsin & Michigan Steamship Co., or the 'W&M' (Wisconsin & Minnesota) in soo_line_wisconsin_central.geojson.
geometry_sources: Main line Quinnesec - Bagley Jct: OpenHistoricalMap way 198645549; Bagley Jct - Peshtigo: OHM 199267330 (both named 'Wisconsin and Michigan Railroad', USGS 3DEP-derived).
Bagley Jct - Menominee: OHM way 198645548 (Milwaukee Road Crivitz - Menominee branch), cross-checked against OSM's live ex-Milwaukee track.
Western Division: OHM way 201212639 (unnamed; identified by mileposts).
Quinnesec - Iron Mountain: OSM way 1529981564 (untagged railway=abandoned) plus a 2.3 mi straight line.
Peshtigo - Peshtigo Harbor: straight line only (6.9 mi).
OHM's dates were never used. OSM carries no old_railway_operator for the W&M under any spelling.
not_yet_sourced: THE PASSENGER END. wm-menominee-faithorn-1920 is a one-year [ANCHOR] [OPEN] (1920 Central States Guide). A combine on the freight 'through the mid-twenties' and caboose riders 'in the final decade' have no year; a 1920s Official Guide, Floyd Schmidt's 'The Wisconsin & Michigan Railway' (c.2017) or Richard McLeod's 1968 R&LHS Bulletin article should settle it. Abandonment (1938; last train 30 Jan 1938 per the michiganrailroads.com history vs an AP item of 5 Aug 1938 quoted in its timeline - conflict recorded) is not a passenger end.
wm-western-division ends [OPEN] at 1910 (last confirmed motor-car year); the true end is 1910-1918.

wm-peshtigo-bagley ends at 1906 and wm-peshtigo-harbor at 1903 - last confirmed years, not known ends (both 1918 at the latest). Whether Peshtigo was served after the 1920 revival is unknown (history vs timeline conflict).
1902 vs 1903 for W&M passenger service to Menominee over the CM&StP - drawn from 1903.
Whether the 1918-1920 shutdown was total: if trains ran Menominee - Faithorn in 1918-19, the 1917 ends could move.
Quinnesec - Iron Mountain: own 4.5 mi line (1909 Commission) vs operation over the Milwaukee (Fowler); the Milwaukee depot site at Iron Mountain is not located.
Norway: which station (W&M 'S.S.' on the spur, or the C&NW 'N.S.') the 1903-17 trains used.
Peshtigo - Peshtigo Harbor is 8.0 mi per Fowler but 6.1 per Wikipedia, and its alignment is unmapped.
Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this layer is an estimate; only the 1903 and 1905 'two round trips' are sourced, and only for those years.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn (report blocks 9-16): Walton - Constine extension (no confirmable passenger years); Koss - Ingalls branch (no passenger evidence; 1895 vs 1902 abandonment conflict); the predecessor Ingalls, White Rapids & Northern (one second-hand 1890 Guide listing, alignment unknown - kept as a lead); the freight-only Aragon Mine, Bergam - Vulcan, Lake Noquebay and Twin Creek branches (Rule 1); the Lake Michigan Car Ferry Transportation Co. barges and the Ann Arbor car-ferry interchange (freight, and boats are not drawn); everything 1918-1919 (operation suspended) and every year after 1920.
metadata.rule4_note: New colour #462080: the W&M had no colour anywhere in data/, and a script confirmed no feature of any company in data/ uses this hex. All eight features share it, including wm-bagley-menominee and the Menominee leg of wm-menominee-faithorn-1920, which run on Milwaukee Road track but carried W&M trains.

properties.line: Wisconsin and Michigan: Bagley Junction – Faithorn Junction
properties.speed_source: estimated: no run time was found for any W&M train; 30 km/h is a guess for a lightly built Upper Peninsula steam road with flag stops every 1-3 mi, not a published average (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap way 198645549 (name 'Wisconsin and Michigan Railroad', source USGS 3DEP; Quinnesec - Bagley Junction, 57.8 mi), traced with opstrace.py. OHM's start_date/end_date (1894-1938, and 1900-1940 'arbitrary' on the Western Division way) were NOT used for any year on this map - geometry only. OpenStreetMap was probed first: no way between 44.9N and 45.9N, 88.2W and 87.5W carries old_railway_operator for the W&M under any spelling (fetch_operator_ways on 'Wisconsin.*Michigan|W&M' returned 0; the area's old_railway_operator values are only C&NW / Chicago and North Western Railway and Soo Line). Waypoints sampled from the OHM line every 2.5 km; Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Bagley Junction - Faithorn Junction: drawn 41.4 mi against a documented 41.2 mi (Fowler, 1906 working-timetable mileposts 62.3 -> 21.1). 100% of the router's mileage is on the OHM way named for the W&M; NO straight-line or approximated leg. Milepost check from Bagley Jct (Fowler vs traced): Walsh 2.9 vs 3.2, Packard 16.3 vs 16.1, Koss 18.9 vs 18.8, Swanson 25.5 vs 25.5, Faithorn Jct 41.2 vs 41.4. Faithorn Junction is cut at the OHM vertex where the W&M crosses OHM's Soo Line way 198645551 (26 m off it), so the line ends on the W&M's own grade, not on the Soo. Alignment era: OHM traces the abandoned grade from USGS mapping, i.e. the line as it was left in 1938; the report records no main-line relocation 1894-1917, but the section near Koss was the regauged Ingalls, White Rapids & Northern formation and any 1894 deviation there is not known.

segments.note: Wisconsin and Michigan Railway. Passenger service began 2 December 1894 from Peshtigo to Faithorn Junction (Wikipedia and the michiganrailroads.com history, both; freight two days later), connecting at Faithorn with Soo Line trains. Until August 1903 this was the heart of the road: Peshtigo (and from 1895 Peshtigo Harbor) - Bagley Jct - Faithorn. Stations Walsh, Kinsman, Packard, Koss (Fisher; Menominee River bridge into Michigan), Kells, Swanson, Everett, Hammond, Bird. Headway 720 min (two trains each way a day) is an ESTIMATE carried back from the August 1903 timetable; no 1894-1902 frequency was found. Walsh control (Oct 1900) changed ownership, not the operator - no Rule 4 split.
sources: Segment-level: taken from research/branches/wisconsin_and_michigan_railway.txt (2026-11-03), not re-checked by the tracer. start 2 Dec 1894 from Wikipedia and the michiganrailroads.com history. Headway NOT SOURCED - estimate.

segments.note: From 16 August 1903 the through trains ran Menominee/Marinette - Bagley Jct - Faithorn - Norway (Quinnesec that autumn, Iron Mountain from June 1908): 'two daily round trips' in August 1903 (michiganrailroads.com history). The 1906 working timetable lists every station Cundy - Peshtigo with flag-stop footnotes (Fowler), and the August 1909 Michigan Railroad Commission inspection found station facilities adequate and a 20-seat gasoline coach giving 'frequent service on some portions of its line'. Receivership 1912-17 and John Marsch's purchase (6 Nov 1917) were changes of ownership with the W&M still running its own trains - no Rule 4 split. Ends 1917: regular passenger trains were 'cut off' c.1918, the Peshtigo shops closed 13 Jan 1918 and the road gave up operation under wartime federal control, so no source shows a passenger train in 1918 itself (the report collapses 'c.1918' inward to 1917). The 1920 revival is drawn separately (wm-menominee-faithorn-1920). Headway 720 min = two round trips a day, from the 1903 announcement; not confirmed for later years.
sources: Segment-level: taken from research/branches/wisconsin_and_michigan_railway.txt (2026-11-03), not re-checked by the tracer. 1903 through service and frequency from the michiganrailroads.com history; 1906 from Fowler's working-timetable note; 1909 from the Michigan Railroad Commission report; end c.1918 (drawn 1917) from the michiganrailroads.com history and the Railroad Signal Engineer quotation there. Headway after 1903 NOT SOURCED - carried forward.

properties.line: Wisconsin and Michigan: Menominee – Faithorn Junction (1920)
properties.speed_source: estimated: no run time was found for any W&M train; 30 km/h is a guess for a lightly built Upper Peninsula steam road with flag stops every 1-3 mi, not a published average (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: Composite of the two features it repeats, vertex for vertex: wm-bagley-menominee (OHM way 198645548, the Milwaukee Road's Crivitz - Menominee branch) reversed, then wm-bagley-faithorn (OHM way 198645549). See those features for method. OHM's start_date/end_date (1894-1938, and 1900-1940 'arbitrary' on the Western Division way) were NOT used for any year on this map - geometry only.
properties.geometry_quality: Menominee - Bagley Junction - Faithorn Junction: drawn 49.8 mi against a documented 49.7 mi (Fowler 70.8 -> 21.1). Menominee - Bagley Jct (8.4 mi) is Milwaukee Road track carrying W&M trains, drawn on OHM's Milwaukee alignment; through Marinette and over the Menominee River it runs within ~150 m of the C&NW for ~2 mi (see wm-bagley-menominee). Bagley Jct - Faithorn Jct is the W&M's own grade. No straight-line leg. Alignment era: the 1920 route north of Faithorn is uncertain (the Faithorn - Aragon Jct rails were lifted Feb 1918 and relaid by end of 1920; the 1920 guide implies Norway was reached via the C&NW station) and is NOT drawn.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] [OPEN] Single proven year. Operation, suspended in 1918 under wartime federal control, resumed in 1920 (michiganrailroads.com timeline), and Fowler cites the 1920 Central States Guide: 'through trains went via Norway N.S. sta, terminating trains started at Norway S.S. sta' - W&M trains in a public guide. Service certainly ran wider than this one year - the history says passengers 'through the mid-twenties could ride as far as the Soo junction in a combine' on the freight, and rode the caboose 'in the final decade' before abandonment in 1938 - but no other year after 1917 is confirmed. 1920 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger carriage actually stopped. Do not widen to 1925 or 1938 without evidence. Headquarters and shops at Menominee from 1918 under John Marsch's ownership (same company - no split). Drawn Menominee - Faithorn only, per the report: where 1920 trains ran north of Faithorn is uncertain. Headway 1440 min (one mixed train a day) is an ESTIMATE; no 1920 frequency was found.
sources: Segment-level: taken from research/branches/wisconsin_and_michigan_railway.txt (2026-11-03), not re-checked by the tracer. 1920 from Fowler's table 39 note citing the 1920 Central States Guide, and the michiganrailroads.com timeline ('resumes' 1920). Any year after 1920 NOT SOURCED. Headway NOT SOURCED - estimate.

properties.line: Wisconsin and Michigan: Peshtigo – Bagley Junction
properties.speed_source: estimated: no run time was found for any W&M train; 30 km/h is a guess for a lightly built Upper Peninsula steam road with flag stops every 1-3 mi, not a published average (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap way 199267330 (name 'Wisconsin and Michigan Railroad', Bagley Junction - Peshtigo), traced with opstrace.py (waypoints every 1.5 km on the OHM line; DP 8 m, trim_reversals). OHM's start_date/end_date (1894-1938, and 1900-1940 'arbitrary' on the Western Division way) were NOT used for any year on this map - geometry only. Nothing in OpenStreetMap is tagged for the W&M here.
properties.geometry_quality: Peshtigo - Bagley Junction: drawn 6.8 mi against a documented 6.0 mi (Fowler 68.3 -> 62.3; Wikipedia 6). 100% on the OHM W&M way; NO straight-line leg. The trace is ~0.85 mi (14%) longer than the milepost difference: it runs to OHM's south end at the C&NW crossing on the south side of Peshtigo (within ~0.3 km of the CN/ex-C&NW track), while the 1906 working timetable's Peshtigo milepost was presumably the W&M depot further north; that depot's location is not known, so the line is not cut short. Alignment era: abandoned-grade trace from USGS mapping; no relocation recorded.

segments.note: Original south end of the W&M: passenger service began 2 December 1894 from Peshtigo (C&NW interchange) to Faithorn Junction. Peshtigo was the southern terminal 1894-1903 and the road's shop town until January 1918. After August 1903 most through trains turned east at Bagley Jct for Marinette/Menominee, but the August 1903 announcement still has trains 'from Norway to Peshtigo harbor', and the 1906 working timetable names Peshtigo with a flag-stop footnote (Fowler) - the last schedule found that does. Drawn to 1906, the last CONFIRMED year; the true end lies between 1906 and 1918 (Peshtigo Harbor - Bagley Jct was torn up in 1918 per the history, while the timeline has Peshtigo - East Norway 'resuming' in 1920 - an unresolved conflict). This is not a known end; do not extend without evidence. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: taken from research/branches/wisconsin_and_michigan_railway.txt (2026-11-03), not re-checked by the tracer. start 2 Dec 1894 from Wikipedia and the michiganrailroads.com history; 1903 from the history's August 1903 timetable announcement; 1906 from Fowler's working-timetable note. End after 1906 NOT SOURCED. Headway NOT SOURCED - estimate.

properties.line: Wisconsin and Michigan: Peshtigo – Peshtigo Harbor
properties.speed_source: estimated: no run time was found for any W&M train; 30 km/h is a guess for a lightly built Upper Peninsula steam road with flag stops every 1-3 mi, not a published average (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: APPROXIMATED - one straight line. Neither OpenStreetMap (no railway=abandoned/razed/demolished, abandoned:railway or rail-trail way between Peshtigo and the bay; fetch_gap returned only the unrelated 'Woods Road Ski Trail') nor OpenHistoricalMap has this line. Drawn from the south end of OHM way 199267330 at Peshtigo to OSM node 368884148 (GNIS 'Peshtigo Harbor', natural=bay).
properties.geometry_quality: Peshtigo - Peshtigo Harbor: ENTIRELY a straight-line approximation, 6.9 mi, against a documented 8.0 mi (Fowler 68.3 -> 76.3; Wikipedia says 6.1 - a source conflict). The real line followed the Peshtigo River down past Place's Rapids to a car-ferry barge slip; its alignment and the exact slip location are not mapped anywhere found. The harbor end is the GNIS bay point, not a documented terminal. (Today's Harbor Road runs the same way and may sit on parts of the grade, but nothing shows it does, so it was not used.)

segments.note: Peshtigo Lumber Company logging line of 1862, bought by the W&M in 1894-95 as its outlet to Green Bay for the Lake Michigan Car Ferry Transportation Co.'s barges to South Chicago (31 Aug 1895 - c.1910), because the W&M could not get dock frontage at Marinette or Menominee. The barges carried freight only - no passenger boat connection is known, and boats are not drawn. Both ends of this span are single-year positive anchors: Place's Rapids appears in the March 1895 Official Guide (Fowler, '3/1895G'), and the August 1903 announcement says trains 'will commence running from Norway to Peshtigo harbor August 16th' (two passenger trains each way). Continuity between them is inferred from the line staying in use as the barge outlet, per the report; a strict reading would be two one-year anchors. 1903 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end (the line was torn up in 1918). The Peshtigo Lumber Co.'s pre-1895 operation had no known passenger service and is not drawn. Headway 1440 min is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: taken from research/branches/wisconsin_and_michigan_railway.txt (2026-11-03), not re-checked by the tracer. 1895 from Fowler table 39 ('Place's Rapids 3/1895G'); 1903 from the michiganrailroads.com W&M timetable page and history. Years 1896-1902 inferred, NOT SOURCED individually. End after 1903 NOT SOURCED. Headway NOT SOURCED - estimate.

properties.line: Wisconsin and Michigan: Bagley Junction – Menominee
properties.speed_source: estimated: no run time was found for any W&M train; 30 km/h is a guess for a lightly built Upper Peninsula steam road with flag stops every 1-3 mi, not a published average (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap way 198645548 (unnamed, source USGS 3DEP: Crivitz - Bagley Junction - Marinette - Menominee, the Milwaukee Road's Crivitz - Menominee branch), traced with opstrace.py on waypoints every 1 km of it; cut 8.5 mi from Bagley Jct. Between Bagley Jct and Marinette it lies 9-40 m from OSM's live ex-Milwaukee track ('Crivitz to Menominee/Marinette subdivision', ways 389126884 / 364266442). OHM's start_date/end_date (1894-1938, and 1900-1940 'arbitrary' on the Western Division way) were NOT used for any year on this map - geometry only.
properties.geometry_quality: Bagley Junction - Menominee: drawn 8.4 mi against a documented 8.5 mi (Fowler 62.3 -> 70.8; the 1938 ICC order's 'about 8.5 miles'). On the Milwaukee Road's track - W&M trains under trackage rights, coloured W&M as the operator. NOT on the C&NW Peninsula Division: Bagley Jct - Marinette (6.7 mi, Fowler 6.7) runs 1.5-9 km from it. Caveat: through Marinette and across the Menominee River into Menominee the Milwaukee and the C&NW ran side by side, and ~2.0 mi of this line lies within 150 m of OSM's CN Marinette Subdivision (ex-C&NW); whether the Milwaukee had its own river bridge or used the C&NW's is not established, so at map scale this stretch is indistinguishable from the C&NW line. Menominee end: cut at the documented 8.5 mi, ~0.4 mi short of where OHM's way stops; the Milwaukee depot's exact site is not known. No straight-line leg. Alignment era: abandoned-grade trace from USGS mapping; no relocation recorded.

segments.note: W&M trains over the Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul's Crivitz - Menominee branch, using the Milwaukee depots at Marinette and Menominee. From 16 August 1903 two daily round trips ran Menominee/Marinette - Bagley Jct - Norway (michiganrailroads.com history). SOURCE CONFLICT on the start: the michiganrailroads.com timeline (1902) says 'Passenger service is extended to Menominee over the CM&St.P railway'; the history dates it 16 Aug 1903. Drawn from 1903, the confirmed one. Menominee became the W&M's headquarters (office 1910, shops 1918) and its interchange with the Ann Arbor car ferries. Ends 1917 with the regular trains (cut off c.1918; see wm-bagley-faithorn); the 1920 anchor is drawn on wm-menominee-faithorn-1920. Trackage rights were surrendered in 1938. Headway 720 min = two round trips a day, from the 1903 announcement; later years NOT confirmed.
sources: Segment-level: taken from research/branches/wisconsin_and_michigan_railway.txt (2026-11-03), not re-checked by the tracer. 1903 start and frequency from the michiganrailroads.com history (1902 per its timeline - conflict recorded); trackage arrangement from Fowler table 40 and the 1938 ICC order as quoted by michiganrailroads.com; end c.1918 (drawn 1917) as wm-bagley-faithorn. Headway after 1903 NOT SOURCED.

properties.line: Wisconsin and Michigan: Faithorn Junction – Quinnesec
properties.speed_source: estimated: no run time was found for any W&M train; 30 km/h is a guess for a lightly built Upper Peninsula steam road with flag stops every 1-3 mi, not a published average (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap way 198645549 (name 'Wisconsin and Michigan Railroad', source USGS 3DEP; Quinnesec - Bagley Junction, 57.8 mi), traced with opstrace.py. OHM's start_date/end_date (1894-1938, and 1900-1940 'arbitrary' on the Western Division way) were NOT used for any year on this map - geometry only. OpenStreetMap was probed first: no way between 44.9N and 45.9N, 88.2W and 87.5W carries old_railway_operator for the W&M under any spelling (fetch_operator_ways on 'Wisconsin.*Michigan|W&M' returned 0; the area's old_railway_operator values are only C&NW / Chicago and North Western Railway and Soo Line). Waypoints sampled from the OHM line every 2.5 km; Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Faithorn Junction - Quinnesec: drawn 16.3 mi against a documented 16.6 mi (Fowler 21.1 -> 4.5). 100% on the OHM way named for the W&M; NO straight-line leg. Milepost check from Faithorn (Fowler vs traced): Loretto 8.5 vs 8.2, Norway 12.7 vs 12.7, Quinnesec 16.6 vs 16.3. On the W&M's own grade throughout, not the C&NW or Milwaukee: the C&NW's Quinnesec line is 0.2-2 km away and only meets it at Quinnesec. Norway: the main line passes ~1 km north of the town centre (the report's 'line proper ran by East Norway'); the W&M's 0.9 mi spur into Norway (OHM way 198645552) is NOT drawn, since which station the 1903-17 trains used is unresolved (report item 7). The 5.6 mi Aragon Mine ('South Norway') branch (OHM 198645553) is freight-only and excluded. Alignment era: abandoned-grade trace from USGS mapping; the Faithorn - Aragon Jct rails were lifted Feb 1918 and relaid by 1920, presumably on the same formation - no relocation is recorded.

segments.note: Extension toward the Menominee Range iron country, built under the Wisconsin, Michigan and Northern charter of 17 Nov 1898 (a paper subsidiary - the W&M ran the trains, no split). Grading began September 1898 and stalled for money until 1903. Trains reached Norway on 16 August 1903 with two daily round trips (michiganrailroads.com history), and Quinnesec 'about two months later', with a stage onward to Iron Mountain until the 1908 extension. Stations Hamlin, Vista, Aragon Junction, Loretto, Norway, Few Mine. Ore from the Aragon and other mines was the point of the line. Ends 1917 with the regular trains (see wm-bagley-faithorn); the route north of Faithorn in 1920 is uncertain and is NOT drawn for 1920. Headway 720 min = two round trips a day, from the 1903 announcement; later years NOT confirmed.
sources: Segment-level: taken from research/branches/wisconsin_and_michigan_railway.txt (2026-11-03), not re-checked by the tracer. 16 Aug 1903 opening to Norway and frequency from the michiganrailroads.com history; Quinnesec autumn 1903 from the same; end c.1918 (drawn 1917) as wm-bagley-faithorn. The MSU 'Making of Modern Michigan' record was not read. Headway after 1903 NOT SOURCED.

properties.line: Wisconsin and Michigan: Quinnesec – Iron Mountain
properties.speed_source: estimated: no run time was found for any W&M train; 30 km/h is a guess for a lightly built Upper Peninsula steam road with flag stops every 1-3 mi, not a published average (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: Partly traced with opstrace.py. Quinnesec (north end of OHM W&M way 198645549) - Cundy - the edge of Kingsford: OpenStreetMap way 1529981564, an untagged railway=abandoned grade that continues the OHM W&M line westward, running ~150-300 m north of and parallel to the CN (ex-C&NW) Iron Mountain Subdivision; it is identified as the W&M's 1908 line by that continuity, NOT by any tag. West of its end (-88.0185) no W&M grade was found in OSM, OHM or the rail-trail layers.
properties.geometry_quality: Quinnesec - Iron Mountain: drawn 4.2 mi against a documented 4.5 mi (Fowler 4.5 -> 0; the 1909 Michigan Railroad Commission's '4.5 miles of new line'). Traced: Quinnesec - Cundy area, 1.7 mi on OSM way 1529981564 (untagged abandoned grade, see geometry_source), reached from the end of the OHM W&M line by a 0.1 mi straight connector. APPROXIMATED: the last 2.3 mi, a straight line from the end of that grade (45.8072N 88.0185W) to the Milwaukee Road (today E&LS 'Channing to Crivitz subdivision') track on the south side of Iron Mountain - it parallels the former C&NW grade ~250 m to its north and is deliberately not snapped onto it. SOURCE CONFLICT on ownership (report item 6): the 1909 Commission says the W&M built its own 4.5 mi; Fowler marks the run 'operated over Milw'; Wikipedia has trackage rights late 1907 and a W&M connection late 1908. Drawn as the W&M's own line ending at the Milwaukee track; the Milwaukee depot the trains used is not located, and the shortfall against 4.5 mi (~0.3 mi) is consistent with the end sitting short of it.

segments.note: Daily service was extended from Quinnesec into Iron Mountain on 14 June 1908 (michiganrailroads.com history), over '4.5 miles of new line ... between Quinnesec and Iron Mountain' (1909 Michigan Railroad Commission report), terminating at the Milwaukee Road passenger station. From 1903 to 1908 passengers went Quinnesec - Iron Mountain by stage or automobile - not rail, not drawn. Ends 1917 with the regular trains (see wm-bagley-faithorn); no later passenger evidence. East Norway - MP 75.8 went to the Milwaukee Road in 1938 for freight. Headway 720 min is carried from the 1903 two-round-trip schedule - an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: taken from research/branches/wisconsin_and_michigan_railway.txt (2026-11-03), not re-checked by the tracer. 14 Jun 1908 start from the michiganrailroads.com history and the 1909 Michigan Railroad Commission report; end c.1918 (drawn 1917) as wm-bagley-faithorn. Headway NOT SOURCED - estimate.

properties.line: Wisconsin and Michigan: Western Division (Everett – Walton)
properties.speed_source: estimated: no run time found; 25 km/h is a guess for a logging-grade branch worked from 1906-10 by a gasoline motor car, not a published average (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap way 201212639 (unnamed, source USGS 3DEP, 27.8 mi from the W&M main line at Everett west past Walton), traced with opstrace.py on waypoints every 2.5 km of it; cut at Walton, 21.9 mi out. Identified as the Western Division by its mileposts, not by any name: it leaves the W&M main line at Everett, crosses the Menominee River at Miscauno Island and crosses the Milwaukee Road (OHM 198645555, today's E&LS) at Holmes Junction. OHM's start_date/end_date (1894-1938, and 1900-1940 'arbitrary' on the Western Division way) were NOT used for any year on this map - geometry only.
properties.geometry_quality: Everett - Walton: drawn 21.9 mi against a documented 22.1 mi (Fowler table 41). 100% on the OHM way; NO straight-line leg. Milepost check from Everett (Fowler vs traced): Miscauno Island 6.6 vs 6.5, Holmes Junction (Milwaukee crossing) 15.4 vs 15.4-15.5, Walton 22.1 vs 21.9. The junction with the main line is at main line MP 25.6 from Quinnesec on Fowler's figures (Everett 30.1) vs 25.05 traced. Walton is located only by today's Walton Road (Town of Dunbar), 0.1 km from the trace; the 5.9 mi on toward Constine is NOT drawn (report block 9, no passenger evidence). Alignment era: the grade was torn up Everett - Pangborn in 1918; OHM traces it from USGS elevation data, i.e. the formation as last built; no relocation recorded.

segments.note: Western Division, built on the Holmes & Sons logging line bought 14 June 1904 and chartered as the Miscauno and North Western (a paper subsidiary - the W&M ran it). 'Western Division passenger service began with two round trips' on 1 January 1905 (michiganrailroads.com history). A 20-passenger gasoline motor car bought in 1906 shuttled guests to the Miscauno Inn on Miscauno Island; the 1909 Official Guide shows Walton as the terminus of service (Fowler, 'Walton 1909G(tm)'), the August 1909 Michigan Railroad Commission report names 'a branch line from Everett to Miscauno', and in 1910 'a motor car replaced train service' - still rail passenger service, so the mode stays intercity_rail. END YEAR IS [OPEN]: 1910 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped before Everett Jct - Pangborn was torn up in 1918. Do not extend without evidence. Mostly a logging line; the extension beyond Walton to Constine had no confirmed passenger service and is not drawn. Headway 720 min = two round trips a day, from the 1905 opening; later frequency NOT confirmed.
sources: Segment-level: taken from research/branches/wisconsin_and_michigan_railway.txt (2026-11-03), not re-checked by the tracer. 1 Jan 1905 start and two round trips from the michiganrailroads.com history; 1909 from Fowler table 41 (1909 Official Guide) and the 1909 Michigan Railroad Commission report; 1910 motor car from the history. End after 1910 NOT SOURCED - [OPEN]. Headway after 1905 NOT SOURCED.
